primary_attribute_value: 12 Megatons TNT (Flattened 80 Million Trees over 2,150 km²)
ended_at: Blast shockwave traveled around Earth twice; glowing skies across Europe for nights
duration_text: Instantaneous superbolide explosion at 5–10 km altitude
casualties_estimate: Estimated 3 fatalities due to remote taiga location; would have vaporized an entire metropolis
economic_damage: Total ecological destruction of 2,150 sq km of Siberian forest
description: The largest cosmic impact event in recorded Earth history. A stony meteoroid or comet nucleus roughly 60 meters wide entered Earth's atmosphere at 54,000 km/h and detonated at an altitude of 5 to 10 km. The 12-megaton shockwave snapped 80 million trees outward in a radial butterfly pattern over 2,150 sq km.
emergencyDirectives: Catalyst for planetary defense networks and United Nations International Asteroid Day (June 30).
plain_language_action_steps: If a superbolide fireball streaks across the sky, immediately move away from windows—the sonic shockwave takes 2-4 minutes to shatter glass inward.
Support global infrared space telescope tracking of near-Earth objects (NEOs).
Heed early planetary defense early-warning deflection and mass shelter alerts.

name: 1989 Hydro-Québec Solar Grid Blackout
primary_attribute_value: Entire Provincial Grid Collapsed in 92 Seconds (6 Million in Dark)
ended_at: Grid collapsed in 92 seconds; power restoration took over 9 hours
duration_text: 92-second cascade collapse; 9 to 24 hours blackout in freezing cold
casualties_estimate: Zero direct; extensive infrastructure freezing damage
description: A major coronal mass ejection caused rapid variations in the Earth's magnetic field. This induced direct current (DC) loops in high-voltage transmission lines, saturating transformers and tripping protective relays in a cascade that collapsed the entire Hydro-Québec electrical grid in just 92 seconds.
emergencyDirectives: Instituted automatic capacitor DC-blocking systems and mandatory space weather alerts for all North American electrical grid operators.
plain_language_action_steps: Keep home emergency battery banks and manual non-electric heaters ready during high solar flare cycles.
Understand that solar storms knock out satellite communication, GPS positioning, and power grids without any rain or wind.
Ensure municipal water treatment stations have dedicated on-site diesel generators.

name: May 2024 Historic G5 Solar Super-Storm (Extreme Auroral Inundation)
primary_attribute_value: NOAA G5 Extreme Geomagnetic Storm (Dst: -412 nT)
magnitude: G5 Extreme (Strongest solar storm since October 2003)
ended_at: Intense coronal bombardment subsided by May 13, 2024
duration_text: 72 hours of intense global auroras and GPS precision degradation
casualties_estimate: Zero injuries; auroras photographed in Florida, India (Ladakh), and Mexico
economic_damage: Agricultural precision GPS tractors knocked offline; Starlink sat communications disrupted
description: Sunspot region 3664 hurled multiple fast-moving coronal mass ejections that collided and merged, striking Earth as a cannibal CME. Triggered the first NOAA G5 Extreme Geomagnetic Storm in over two decades, painting pink and green auroras across the sky in tropical and mid-latitude regions like Ladakh (India), Florida, and the Mediterranean.
emergencyDirectives: Power grids successfully implemented mitigation procedures; commercial aviation rerouted away from polar orbits.
plain_language_action_steps: Expect agricultural, maritime, and drone precision GPS to experience positional errors of several meters during G5 geomagnetic storms.
Take advantage of night sky dark-sky parks to witness extraordinary natural auroral displays.
Check space weather alerts before undertaking precision drone or satellite surveying operations.
